The implementation details diverge significantly between the two primary SGS variants [S2][S3, unofficial].

The claim states that implementation details diverge significantly between the two variants. Source [S2] describes 'Stochastic Gaussian Splatting' (SGS) as a framework for uncertainty estimation using Variational Inference, where Gaussian parameters (mean, covariance, opacity, color) are treated as random variables sampled from distributions, and the rendering pipeline is extended to support Monte Carlo sampling for uncertainty. Source [S3] describes 'Gaussian Point Splatting' as a stochastic method for rendering massive scenes by sampling opaque points from Gaussians and using 64-bit atomics to eliminate sorting and tile-based rendering bottlenecks. The core implementation details differ fundamentally: [S2] focuses on probabilistic modeling and uncertainty via VI and reparameterization within a standard splatting pipeline, while [S3] focuses on high-performance rendering of massive scenes by replacing deterministic sorting with stochastic point sampling and atomic operations. Thus, the evidence supports that their implementation details diverge significantly.
